thread:
john (Customer): Hey @maria — our private deployment in prod (VPC-237a) started failing inference streams around 09:12 UTC. Clients see repeated TLS handshake failures and ECONNRESET. Example from client: 'tlsv1 alert unknown ca' and 'connection reset by peer'. Any quick checks?

maria (Support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a couple of logs and a curl from a host in your VPC? Also which model/hostname and whether this is behind a NAT/firewall?

john (Customer): Host: inference.private.redwood-corp.internal:443. Model: redwood-embedded-13b (v2). From app host: 
```
> curl -v --resolve inference.private.redwood-corp.internal:443:10.0.1.45 https://inference.private.redwood-corp.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.1.45 (10.0.1.45) port 443 (#0)
* Empty reply from server
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
```
Openssl: 
```
> openssl s_client -connect 10.0.1.45:443 -servername inference.private.redwood-corp.internal
... SSL handshake ...
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
... TLS alert: unknown ca
```
And tcpdump from the app host shows RSTs:
```
10:12:03.123456 IP 10.0.5.23.49158 > 10.0.1.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0], length 0
10:12:03.223789 IP 10.0.1.45.443 > 10.0.5.23.49158: Flags [R], seq 1, ack 1, win 0, length 0
10:12:03.323101 IP 10.0.5.23.49158 > 10.0.1.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, ...
```

maria (Support): Hmm. RSTs from 10.0.1.45 — is that the inference host or a NAT/firewall? If your NAT changes source port outside your allowed ephemeral range, return packets may be dropped by a NACL. Can you run: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -n 'tcp and (port 443 or portrange 49152-65535)' -c 50
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
```
and paste the first 20 lines? Also tell us your outbound NACL ephemeral port range.

lee (Infra): Noting the RSTs come from the transit/firewall EIP — looks like upstream is terminating or actively rejecting. Could be DNAT/inspection or an intermediate proxy.

john (Customer): 10.0.1.45 is our transit VPC firewall EIP. We recently hardened the outbound NACL to only allow ephemeral ports 49160-49200. Looks like client ephemeral was 49158 which is below the allowed range.

maria (Support): That aligns — asymmetry: client chooses 49158, NAT/translation may map or keep it and then return path denied by NACL because 49158 isn't allowed. Two remediation options: expand your outbound NACL ephemeral range to the full IANA default (49152-65535) or, if your NAT implementation supports it, configure the NAT to allocate source ports inside your allowed window consistently. Also check any inline TLS DPI that might rewrite SNI or certs.

security-bot: Alert: recent change by alice at 3623455000 — updated NACL outbound ephemeral ports to 49160-49200 (policy 2187).

john (Customer): Ok that makes sense. One more weirdness: why did openssl report unknown_ca? We use a customer-managed CA for mTLS — could the firewall/proxy be intercepting?

maria (Support): unknown_ca can be a client-side effect when a handshake is truncated or when an inline proxy presents a different cert chain. If the TCP handshake is being reset mid-way, the client may surface certificate errors. After you widen the ephemeral port range, retest the TLS handshake end-to-end. Recommended tests after change: 
```
# from inside the same subnet as your app
curl -v --resolve inference.private.redwood-corp.internal:443:10.0.1.45 https://inference.private.redwood-corp.internal/health
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.1.45:443 -servername inference.private.redwood-corp.internal -showcerts
# or check from control plane to verify server cert
curl -v --header 'Host: inference.private.redwood-corp.internal' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/model/ping
```
If you still see different certs, capture a server-side tcpdump on the inference host to confirm whether a proxy is terminating TLS.

john (Customer): Expanding NACL now to include 49152-65535. Will run tests and report back.

deploy-bot: transit-firewall config update applied (changed NACL outbound range) — rollout finished at 3623456800.

john (Customer): Re-tested after NACL change: streaming and handshake stable, no TLS unknown_ca errors, no upstream RSTs seen. Thanks for the guidance! :tada:

maria (Support): Awesome — glad to hear it. We'll keep this open for 24h to monitor. Suggested postmortem items: why the NAT port allocation drifted vs. NACL assumption, and add runbook entry to require ephemeral NACLs include 49152-65535 for inference egress. If you'd like we can schedule a short RCA call.

lee (Infra): Noted — will add a guardrail to the infra templates so future default hardened NACLs include the full ephemeral range for VPCs that host inference clients.

john (Customer): Sounds good, thanks everyone!"
